name: Motor Assisted Scooter
description: A self-propelled device with handlebars, a deck to stand on or a seat to sit on, an electric motor of not more than 2,000 W, a top speed of 20 mph and the ability to be moved by human power alone; a seated electric two-wheeler too powerful to be an e-bike but held to 20 mph lands here.

restrictions.rule: At least two wheels, working brakes, handlebars, and either a standing deck or a seat to sit, straddle or stand on
An electric motor not exceeding 2,000 W and a top speed of 20 mph on a paved level surface, and designed to be propelled by human power alone
Not an electric assisted bicycle, moped, motorcycle or motor vehicle

Sellers must disclose at sale and in any advertising, website or social media post, in bold capitals at least the size of its description, that it is not an electric assisted bicycle but a motor vehicle subject to motor vehicle laws, and that insurance may not cover it

Commercial sellers must disclose at sale and in any advertising, website or social media post, in bold capitals, that it is not an electric assisted bicycle but a motor vehicle subject to motor vehicle laws, that a helmet may be required, and that insurance may not cover it
restrictions.citation: Utah Code §§41-6a-1115.5(8), 41-6a-1511(6), as amended and enacted by H.B. 381 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Ridden under the rules for bicycles, with no driver's license, registration or insurance
May not be ridden faster than 15 mph, in a public parking structure, where bicycles are prohibited, with more riders than it's designed for, or after being altered from the manufacturer's design
May not be ridden on a freeway
restrictions.citation: Utah Code §41-6a-1115, as amended by H.B. 381 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Riders under 21 must wear a helmet meeting 16 CFR part 1203 on a highway, except on one rented from a business
Riders under 8 may not ride with the motor running on public property, a highway, path or sidewalk
Riders under 8 may not ride on a highway with the motor running
restrictions.citation: Utah Code §41-6a-1115, as amended by H.B. 381 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Riders 8 to 15 may ride on a highway with the motor running only under a parent's or responsible adult's direct supervision or with a personal electric vehicle safety certificate, and riders 16 and older ride unsupervised
restrictions.citation: Utah Code §41-6a-1115, as amended by H.B. 381 (2026)

restrictions.rule: May use a crosswalk, but not negligently or faster than is reasonable
A peace officer who sees a rider under 18 commit a violation may hold the scooter and release it only to a parent or guardian
